page: Amazon Web Services r7a.medium is a memory-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features a single dedicated physical core and vCPU from an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor operating at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a high 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reflect its single-core configuration. The server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, due to having only one vCPU, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core score in the bottom 10% to 25%. Memory bandwidth write speeds for large blocks and single-threaded gzip compression perform at average levels, while read-only memory bandwidth and database operations score in the lower percentiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7a.medium offers an entry-level entry point into the DDR5 memory-optimized class without the overhead of multi-core licensing or resource density. It is best suited for lightweight memory-bound workloads that do not require parallel processing, such as small-scale caching, single-threaded text processing, or basic memory-intensive utility scripts.
